The article itself uses the 2014 Sony hack as an example of a state-sponsored cyber attack against the US. It is difficult, if not impossible, to reliably attribute an attack to a party or state. And even if it were possible, I wouldn't trust our government to do it properly (or honestly).

Next, the issue of equivocation. Cyber warfare isn't actually "warfare", and it is misleading to call it such. Politicians - like HRC, for example - are quick to equate cyber attacks (which again, cannot be reliably attributed) with actual attacks, and call for military intervention as a result.

The NSA "ramping up" (as though it weren't already executing offensive operations the world over) is just another way they'll pull us into conflict after conflict after war.
